Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS : 2489 - 1963 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
BABY WEIGHING MACHINES 

0. FOREWORD 

0*! This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institu- 
tion on 17 September 1963, after the draft finalized by the Commercial 
Weights and Measures Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Engineering Division Council. 

0.2 The capacity for the baby weighing machine has been laid down as 
10, 15 or 20 kg. 

0,3 This specification is one of a series of Indian Standards for commercial 
metric weights and measures being prepared by the Indian Standards 
Institution. 

0.4 Wherever a reference to any Indian Standard appears in this speci- 
fication, it shall be taken as a reference to the latest version of the 
standard. 

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, ex- 
pressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance 
with IS : 2-1960 Rules for Rounding Oflf Numerical Values {Revised), 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should 
be the same as that of the specified value in this standard, 

0.6 This standard is intended chiefly to cover the technical provisions 
relating to baby weighing machines; and it does not include all the 
necessary provisions of a contract. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the requirements for baby weighing machines. 

2. DEFINITION 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, a baby weighing machine shall mean 
a weighing machine with a pan to receive the baby to be weighed. A 
typical baby weighing machine is illustrated in Fig. 1 . 



i^ms^mi 



PC>.v« 



wm 



IS : 2489 - 1963 

3. CAPACITY 

3,1 The machines shall have a maximum capacity of 10) 15 or 20 kg, as 
specified by the purchaser. 

4. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

4.1 The machinesr shall comply with the general requirements specified in 
IS : 1432-1959 General Requirements for Weighing Instruments. In 
addition, the machines shall comply with the requirements given in 4*2 
to 4^. 

4.2 The pan for che baby shall be either an oval or a rectangular basin, 
or an open-ended trough of the following approximate dimensions: 





Minimum Dimensi< 




mm 


Length 
Width 


550 
300 


Depth: 
Basin type 
Trough type 


100 

125 



4,2.1 The pan shall be smooth, non-porous, readily cleanable and of 
adequate strength and should preferably be made of a low heat-conduct- 
ing material. Wicker*work shall not be used in the construction of the 
pan. 

4*3 Counter type baby weighing machines shall be provided with hard 
rubber or fibre stops to prevent noise or * jar ' in the out-of-balance 
position. 

4*4 All machines shall be so constructed as to enable a direct net weighing 
to be obtained. 

4*5 Baby weighing machines of thespring-balance> self-indicating or semi- 
self-indicating types shall be fitted with efficient oscillation control devices. 

4.6 In spring-balance, self-indicating or semi-self-indicating type of baby 
weighing machines, the dial shall be graduated into equal parts and the 
minimum distance between consecutive graduations shall be not less than 
2 mm. Provision of a screw for adjustment of the pointer to correct zero 
error shall also be provided. 

4.6.1 The extremity of the pointer shall not exceed 1*0 mm in width 
and shall be not more than 3*0 mm away from the graduations on the 
dial. The weight corresponding to the interval between consecutive 
graduation marks shall not exceed 50 g* 



IS : 2489 - 1963 

4.7 The base of the machine shall be wide and heavy to avoid tilting and 
the position of the index, when there is no load, shall be clearly indicated 
by a zero mark. 

4.8 When the weighing machine is provided with an adjustable pointer, 
the range of adjustment shall not exceed one percent of the capacity of 
the machine. 

5, TESTS 

5.1 In spring-balance, self-indicating or scmi*self-indicating type of 
machines, the permissible error shall not exceed the weight corresponding 
to half the interval between consecutive graduations, 

5.2 When a load equal to half the capacity of the machine is placed at 
the farthest point from the centre of the pan and the other half at any 
position, the machine shall be correct to the prescribed limit of error. 

5.3 Each graduation of the machine shall be tested. 

5.4 For counter type machines, the sensitivity and the greatest eiTor shall 
be as under: 

Capacity Sensitiveness when Greatest Error in Excess 

Fully Loaded or Deficiency when Fully 

Loaded 

kg g g 

10 70 105 

15 80 12-0 

20 90 13-5 

5.5 The machine shall be correct whether the test is made by progressively 
increasing or decreasing loads provided that in either case the machine is 
allowed to vibrate before the reading is taken. 

5*6 The spring-balance type machines shall be loaded to its full capacity 
and the load maintained for a period of 24 hours after which it shall be 
removed. Four hours after removal of the load, the balance shall not 
show any permanent set. Further, when tested as stated in 5.5, it shall 
record correct readings. 

6. SEALING 

6«1 Each machine shall be provided with a plug or stud of soft metal on 
a conspicuous part of the beam or the body for receiving a seal. Such a 
plug or stud shall be made irremovable by underctUting it or by some 
other suitable method.
